cover: Migrant boat sinks; at least 34 dead
Storm collapses sandbank on tents; 5 dead
Army detains ICC suspect Ahmed Haroun
No protest request accepted in 2 months
hope_caption:
Israel released Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after five days' detention without charge; his lawyers say the suspicion rested on a public podcast conversation.
Source: Al Jazeera

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: A migrant boat capsizes
bullets: The pirogue sank off northwestern Senegal on Saturday.
Senegal's interior ministry says one person was rescued.
635 people died on the route to the Canaries in five months, a rights group says.
stories.caption:
Most of the dead came from two districts of Kébémer, local press reports. Boats from West Africa head for Spain's Canary Islands.
Source: Al Jazeera

stories.label: World · Civilian harm
stories.head: Rain brings down a sandbank on tents
bullets: Local health authorities say four of the five dead were children.
Storms flooded about 70,000 tents, Gaza's media office says.
Save the Children blames Israeli limits on shelter; no Israeli response reported.
stories.caption:
Civil Defence says 300,000 tents are needed and it took over 1,500 emergency calls during the storm.
Source: Al Jazeera

stories.label: World · Due process
stories.head: Army detains Ahmed Haroun
bullets: Wanted by the ICC over alleged Darfur crimes; he denies the charges.
His lawyers and party confirmed the detention; reports differ on where.
No army comment; the military refused past ICC handovers.
stories.caption:
Rights lawyers have urged the army to hand him to the ICC. He had walked out of prison during the war.
Source: AP

stories.label: India · Assembly
stories.head: Nowhere to protest in Delhi
bullets: None of 15 protest applications since 5 Sep was accepted, a police officer says.
Police named Burari, Ramlila and CBD grounds as alternatives.
Groups say getting permission there has proved hard.
stories.caption:
A student union's protest on Manipur never happened after Jantar Mantar was taken off the list on 9 October.
Source: Indian Express
